newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Bundesbank must respect parliament.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Bundesbank must respect parliament.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Saturday the Bundesbank, now in open opposition to Bonn's plan to revalue its gold stocks to qualify for Europe's monetary union (EMU), should respect parliament's independence to pass and change laws.

Waigel's comment to journalists was a pointed reminder to the Bundesbank that its fabled independence, which the central bank demonstrated by rejecting his gold plan on Wednesday, is based on a law that the Bonn parliament has the power to change.

"I expect the Bundesbank to respect the legislative independence of politics just as politics always respects the independence of the Bundesbank in monetary policy," he said at this resort in southern Germany.
"I have no problems with Hans Tietmeyer," he added, referring to the president of the Bundesbank.
Waigel said Bonn would fill yawning holes in its 1997 budget through spending cuts and privatisations.

He also said he saw no opposition in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democratic parliamentary faction to his plan to change the Bundesbank law. Parliament is due to begin debating a draft law to change the Bundesbank statutes next Thursday.
